capabilities.wealth_summary: Mashreq runs wealth through the Retail Banking Group (Group Head Fernando Morillo): Mashreq Private Banking (Vipul Kapur, also responsible for Wealth Products & Platform), the Mashreq Gold affluent tier (AED 500k relationship balance) and the NEO retail app. Private banking offers advisory, discretionary mandates (in-house via Mashreq Capital plus Goldman Sachs Asset Management discretionary portfolios since Apr 2025), 150+ funds from 30+ fund houses on an open-architecture platform, structured products, bonds/sukuk, 19,000+ securities in 37 markets (TraderPro app; FinIQ platform for RMs), Lombard lending and an EAM desk. In Jun 2026 it executed a private-markets (pre-IPO) investment through an ADGM fund managed by Neovision on Red Lions Capital's Digital Investment Platform, with Allfunds integration. NEO offers UAE equities via Mashreq Securities, 3,000+ US stocks/ETFs via DriveWealth from USD 1, mutual funds from USD 100 and three ETF portfolios (Conservative/Balanced/Growth) 'curated by leading asset managers, including BlackRock'. Mashreq Capital (DFSA) runs six to seven public funds, incl. the BITMAC fund with 5% Bitcoin (Dec 2025). No AUM is disclosed.

private_banking.detail: Mashreq Private Banking (Dubai): RM plus investment and insurance specialists, five-step investment process, discretionary mandates, fixed income, equities, funds, structured products, FX and precious-metal trading, bespoke and Lombard lending, family-office services (legacy planning, trusts and wills, tax and estate planning via third parties), EAM coverage team. Won Global Private Banking Innovation Awards 2026 (Best Private Bank - Middle East and UAE).

asset_management.detail: Mashreq Capital (DIFC) Limited, 100%-owned, incorporated in DIFC 7 Feb 2006, DFSA-regulated: conventional and Shariah-compliant DIFC-domiciled funds (Conventional Equity Fund 2005, Conventional FI Fund 2006, Sukuk Fund 2009, Islamic fixed income fund, Global Portfolios Conservative/Balanced/Growth, BITMAC multi-asset fund with 5% gold and 5% Bitcoin via ETFs, launched 3 Dec 2025 from USD 100) and discretionary accounts. AUM not disclosed. CEO Philip Philippides since Nov 2024.

brokerage.detail: Mashreq Securities LLC (100%): DFM, ADX and Nasdaq Dubai trading in the app, digital NIN creation, IPO access. International: 19,000+ securities across 37 markets via Mashreq TraderPro app; EAM page cites 24/7 equity trading across 32 markets. US stocks/ETFs in NEO via DriveWealth LLC (Mashreq acts as introducing broker).

digital_investing.detail: Mashreq Mobile App / NEO Investments: UAE equities, international equities, 3,000+ US stocks and ETFs from USD 1 (fractional on market orders; first 10 trades a month free, then 0.20%, min USD 1), mutual funds from USD 100, Gold & Silver Edge Account, and three diversified ETF portfolios from USD 100. Launch dates not stated.

advisory.detail: Private Banking investment specialists and RMs; Mashreq Gold relationship team; FinIQ platform used by RMs for offline access to international markets.

discretionary.detail: Discretionary mandates (packaged, customised and tailored portfolios) managed by Mashreq Capital using asset allocation from an international asset manager; Goldman Sachs Asset Management discretionary portfolios offered to wealth clients from Apr 2025 ('exclusive tie-up' per EAM page).

model_portfolios_robo.detail: NEO diversified portfolios (Conservative: global bond ETFs; Balanced; Growth: global equities) from USD 100, 'curated by leading asset managers, including BlackRock'. Mashreq Capital also lists Global Portfolios (Conservative/Balanced/Growth). Not described as a robo-advisor.

funds_platform.detail: Open-architecture fund platform: 150+ active and passive funds from 30+ global fund houses (none named), plus in-house Mashreq Capital funds; 24x7 digital subscription/redemption from USD 100. Platform provider not named.

structured_products.detail: Listed under Private Banking investments; EAM page offers structuring across equities, rates, fixed income and commodities. Terms not published.

private_markets.detail: Jun 2026: private-markets (pre-IPO) investment executed for HNW and family-office clients through an ADGM-domiciled fund managed by Neovision Wealth Management on Red Lions Capital's Digital Investment Platform, with Allfunds integration; Kapur described it as strengthening an 'existing private equity offering'. EAM page cites private placement solutions.

islamic_wealth.detail: Mashreq Capital Sukuk Fund and Shariah-compliant fixed income fund with Shari'ah Supervisory Board; Shariah-compliant stocks on the international equities platform; sukuk trading via EAM desk; Mashreq Al Islami window.

open_items: X13 people pass (2026-10-12): 2025-2026 role-based news checks run for every decision-maker (17 WebSearch calls; no 403/406 on mashreq.com). LinkedIn: the search tool declines name-based look-ups and mashreq.com links no personal profiles, so the URLs for Abdelaal and Morillo are kept from the original workbook; new URLs recorded for Bhatia (link on S51) and Shitole (search result, S64). Nothing found for Kapur, Fouad, Kajiji, Philippides, Abdel Razek and Xi Liang.

FY2025 Annual Report (S44) opens with tools/pdftext.py (11.75 MB, 129 PDF pages); X13 used only its governance section. Its other content (the ~85.6% Al Ghurair figure, customer and employee numbers, Mashreq Capital fund count) was not used in this people pass — fill in a later metrics pass.

Resolved in X13: the management-team index page renders no names (JavaScript), but the UAE site map lists 23 individual profile pages; Abdel Razek's profile is at .../management-team/mohamed-abdul/ (S58) and AR 2025 confirms him in the role, so the 'Ellis Wang' aggregator listing is contradicted.

Lead check: 'Neovision' and 'Red Lions' are Neovision Wealth Management Ltd (ADGM/FSRA fund manager) and Red Lions Capital (research/technology, Digital Investment Platform), per a 9 Jun 2026 GlobeNewswire release issued by Neovision. The release was not found on mashreq.com news. The target company and deal size were not disclosed.
Lead check: the ~85.6% Al Ghurair ownership was not confirmed (see discrepancies).
Lead check: BlackRock is named only as a curator of NEO investment solutions. Whether the three NEO portfolios are BlackRock model portfolios is not stated.

Head of Mashreq Securities still not identified (no official page names one). Mufazzal Kajiji (Head of Mashreq Gold, 2020) still unconfirmed: no official page names a Head of Mashreq Gold and no 2025-2026 mention was found (status Requires verification). Radu Topliceanu left NEO in Feb 2026; successor Jayant Bhatia (Aug 2026) added from news — no mashreq.com release found.

Mashreq Capital AUM: Forbes Middle East's Top 50 Asset Managers 2026 (S62) states USD 1.34bn AUM in FY2025 — a Forbes figure, not issuer-disclosed; not recorded as a metric in the X13 people pass. Consider in a metrics pass.
Private banking entry threshold not published.
Original relationship contacts (Alvaro Cuesta Sanchez, Mahvish Jaffer, Vickram Lal) could not be confirmed from public sources. Their internal emails were not copied.

Mashreq Capital's leadership page (S66) and news page render no names or items (JavaScript); its board, management team (other than the CEO and the Head of Fixed Income) and Shariah Supervisory Board members are not identified. Amol Shitole has no published biography.
Xi Liang (Head of AI, Jul 2025): no 2026 source and not on the official roster; re-check in the next pass.

Official management-team roster (site map, 2026-10-12) and AR 2025 also cover executives not profiled here (outside the people-pass scope): Anuratna Chadha (Group Chief Risk Officer, 2019), Tarek El Nahas (Group Head of International Banking, 2020), Mark Edwards (Group Head of Operations, 2020), Roy Sebastian (Group Chief Credit Officer, 2018), Scott Ramsay (Group Head of Compliance & Bank MLRO, 2020), Rania Nerhal (Group Chief Client Experience and Conduct Officer, 2018), Hamda Alshamali (Group Chief People & Intellectual Capital Officer, 2022), Muna Bin Ghurair (Group Head of Marketing & Corporate Communications, 2022), Hassan Ali (Group Chief of Internal Audit, 2023), Bassam Moussa (Group General Counsel, 2023), Ibrahim AlMheiri (CEO of Mashreq Al Islami & Head of Islamic Banking, undated), Shaima Al Obeidli (Group Company Secretary, May 2022). The 'alexander-raiff' profile page carries no biography and the 'marouf-mohamed-shweikeh' page (Group General Counsel) appears superseded by Moussa's. Other directors at 31 Dec 2025 (AR 2025): Rashed Saif Ahmed Al Ghurair (2013), Saeed Saif Al Ghurair (2021; BNCC chair), Mariam Ghobash (2024; independent; BRCESGC chair), Iyad Malas (2021; BCC chair), John Iossifidis (2021; independent; BAC chair).

Pages that returned no readable text on 2026-10-12: Albawaba report on Morillo's appointment as Head of Retail Banking Group (date and prior role unconfirmed; AR 2025 gives 2024), the Singapore FinTech Festival speaker page (S49) and HR Today (S52). Gulf News, Forbes Middle East, Fintech News UAE and the Dubai Media Office opened normally.
